advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a publish_autodeploy_marker_delta AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE call in observability.sh (or correct the comments/commit that claim it is already published).
evidence: autodeploy.sh:228 comment: 'AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE marker so observability.sh can publish it as a metric.'
observability.sh:216-219 only call publish_autodeploy_marker_delta for AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED and AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT
search across repo: AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE appears only in autodeploy.sh and the new test; no observability.sh / terraform reference exists (ABSENCE)
advisory.finding: The new AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE journal marker has no consumer: observability.sh publishes marker deltas only for AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED and AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT, so despite comments/commit message claiming 'observability.sh can publish it as a metric', no CloudWatch metric is emitted for this token in this change.
scenarios: disk pressure recurs and the marker fires, but no metric/alarm ever reflects it because the publisher was never added
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a publish_autodeploy_marker_delta AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE <metric> <offset_file> <label> invocation in observability.sh §4a alongside the existing two, and a corresponding alarm if intended.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the throttle should arm on prune ATTEMPT or on prune SUCCESS; the marker text 'attempt' is tested, but confirm arming-before-prune is the intended behavior under a failing daemon.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:244: prune_docker_caches (runs AFTER the timestamp write)
prune_docker_caches only logs on failure and returns 0 (autodeploy.sh:206-214), so a failing prune is indistinguishable from a successful one to the throttle
advisory.finding: The throttle timestamp (PRESSURE_PRUNE_TS_FILE) and the countable marker are written BEFORE prune_docker_caches runs, so if the prune fails the throttle is still armed for the full PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL and the next tick will not retry despite sustained pressure.
scenarios: docker daemon is wedged under pressure: the prune times out/fails, but the throttle still blocks the next ~600s of ticks from retrying, prolonging disk pressure

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion to the throttle test that `_markers(result, "AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE")` is empty when the prune is throttled.
evidence: test_throttle_suppresses_a_second_prune_within_the_interval asserts only `"builder-prune" not in commands and "image-prune" not in commands` (test line 219) with no `_markers(result, "AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE")` check

autodeploy.sh:237-240 the throttle branch logs and `return 0` BEFORE the `marker AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` call at autodeploy.sh:241 — so marker suppression on throttle is a distinct behavior this test does not bind
the marker is the observability signal published as a metric (autodeploy.sh:227-228 comment): emitting it on a throttled tick would over-count without failing any current test
advisory.finding: The throttle test asserts only that no prune ran; it does not assert the countable AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE marker is suppressed on the throttled tick. Since the throttled branch returns before the marker emit (autodeploy.sh:238-240 precede :241), a regression that emitted the marker on every throttled tick would over-count the alarm metric yet still pass this test.
scenarios: A refactor moves the `marker` emit above the throttle check, causing a marker on every no-op tick while disk stays high

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a boundary test that pct == DISK_PRESSURE_PCT (e.g. 80 with DISK_PRESSURE_PCT=80) triggers the prune and marker.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:232 `if [ "$pct" -lt "$DISK_PRESSURE_PCT" ]; then return 0` — the equality boundary is decided here
tests set pct to 90 (test line 179/210/230), 88 (test line 246), 70 (test line 195): no case exercises pct == DISK_PRESSURE_PCT
advisory.finding: The exact at/above boundary (root pct == DISK_PRESSURE_PCT) is untested. The stated contract is 'at/above DISK_PRESSURE_PCT' and the code uses `[ "$pct" -lt "$DISK_PRESSURE_PCT" ]` (autodeploy.sh:232), but all tests use strictly-above (90, 88) or below (70) values, so an off-by-one regression to `-le` would go undetected.
scenarios: Disk sits exactly at the threshold percent; a regression flipping `-lt` to `-le` (or vice versa) changes whether the reclaim fires
